Record carries a 'version' field that increments on every successful write (observed 1 -> 2 -> 3 across edit + revert) -- looks like optimistic-locking support, but whether a stale/mismatched version is REJECTED was not tested (edge case matrix row 12 in KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md). Strip the nested carrierInfo object before PUT, it is a read-only expansion. VERSION FIELD IS NOT OPTIMISTIC LOCKING (settled live 2026-08-11): PUT with a deliberately stale version (sent 1 while the stored record was at 2) was ACCEPTED -- 200, the change applied, version bumped to 3. No 409, no error. So `version` is a write counter only and this API offers NO lost-update protection: two workers editing the same record silently clobber each other. Any concurrent executor must serialise per-record itself.

Columns owned by the supplier row persist normally: trustedFlag, autoReceiveFlag, trackConsignment, consignmentDays, consignmentType, receiveStatus, addressId. Worse, two of them are ALIASES: supplier.receivingPhone IS address.phoneNumber and supplier.receivingFax IS address.faxNumber -- writing them under the supplier field name never works under any circumstance. To change them: PUT /data/WM/wm/addresses/{addressId} with phoneNumber / faxNumber. Proven on a supplier created in-app seconds earlier, so it is NOT about EDI-synced records; the original test just happened to pick an address-owned field.
